<thought>We need to determine how many methyl (CH₃) groups are present in the unknown molecule. The most direct way is to obtain its ¹H NMR spectrum, which will show signals for methyl protons (typically singlets, doublets, etc., around 0.8–1.2 ppm) along with integration values that indicate the number of equivalent protons. By analyzing the number of distinct methyl signals and their integration, we can count the total methyl groups. I will request the proton NMR spectrum for the sample.</thought>
